A federal judge in California has barred the Trump Administration
from threatening election workers.
Jew Joffee Block reports the order comes as federal officials
have been escalating their feud with California election officials.

in California and Washington they could be criminally prosecuted

A coalition that includes unions that represent election workers

Jew Joffee Block, NPR News.
President Trump won Michigan in 2024,
and now Democrats are trying to hang onto an open seat.

Democrats here nominated former public health official Abdul El-Sayed,
testing how a Democrat from the party's left flank will fare in a purple state.

accusing him without evidence of ties to terrorist groups.
My whole family, or the uniform of the United States of America,

Sam Greenglass, NPR News, in Hanover and Wyandotte, Michigan.
Protesters are out in force in France again,
angry over the rising cost of living and education,
though the protests have been mostly peaceful today.
Tens of thousands of police have been deployed around the country,
and France's Interior Minister says there's a risk of problems,

And Piers Eleanor Beardsley is out among the protesters in Paris.
This is the third weekend that people have come out on a Saturday.
Officials were nervous this time.
The Interior Minister even said there was a high chance of violence

calling on people to come out and party and "start a revolution."
Some of them were rather menacing,
so the authorities put massive security on the streets.
70,000 police, also helicopters, drones, water cannons, armored vehicles.
They were really ready for everything.
But this protest here in Paris is wrapping up very peacefully.
And Piers Eleanor Beardsley in Paris, you're listening to NPR News.
Deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo have passed 5,000.
Congo's Ministry of Health data shows the disease has killed nearly 50 percent of those infected,
raising concern from health experts in the country's ability to contain the deadly virus.
This is officials' struggle with tracing contacts.
The latest outbreak, the second deadliest Ebola outbreak in history,
was caused by the Bandi Bugyo virus, which is declared in May
and has no known vaccine or treatment.
The World Health Organization, though, says testing and clinical vaccine trials are underway.
Cases have also been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda.
Tomorrow marks the end of daylight saving time.
Many Americans will turn their clocks back one hour.
And Piers Ava Berger reports that the future of the more than a century-long practice, though, is uncertain.
An extra hour of sleep is just a day away.
At 2 a.m. Sunday morning, many clocks across the country will be sent backwards one hour.
This twice-yearly change has once again become political.
According to a Gallup poll from last year, more than half of Americans want daylight saving time gone.
President Donald Trump agrees.
He wants to make daylight saving time permanent.
That means the clocks won't change.
Here's what he told auto workers during a July speech in Michigan.
Let's get rid of daylight saving time stuff, OK?
A bipartisan bill to do just that, the Sunshine Protection Act, is stuck in the Senate.
So tomorrow, the clocks will still jump back.
Ava Berger, NPR News.
